<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest  Expense.</i>&#160; Interest expense consists of interest  associated with the Company&#146;s revolving line of credit, term loan, convertible  notes and other debt as described in the notes to the Company&#146;s financial  statements contained elsewhere in this Report.&#160;  As a result of the Company&#146;s proposed public offering, the Company  expects that, when the proposed offering is completed and the net proceeds are  applied to the intended uses, its debt levels will be substantially lower than  their current levels which resulted from the acquisition of Bobcat on December  16, 2005.&#160; The Company also expects that  its effective borrowing rate will be substantially less than that associated  with the outstanding convertible subordinated debt intended to be converted to  equity in connection with the proposed public offering.&#160; Accordingly, subsequent to the proposed
public offering, interest expense is expected to be substantially lower than  the levels of interest expense following the Company&#146;s acquisition of  Bobcat.&#160; There can be no assurance that  the proposed public offering will be completed.&#160; Interest income primarily consists of interest earned on the  Company&#146;s cash balances.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation  Expense.</i>&#160; The Company&#146;s depreciation expense is based  on estimates, assumptions and judgments relative to capitalized costs, useful  lives and salvage values of the Company&#146;s assets. The Company generally  computes depreciation using the straight-line method.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Income  Taxes</i>.&#160; At December 31, 2005, the Company had  approximately $29.2 million of net operating losses (&#147;NOLs&#148;) available to  offset future taxable income.&#160; These  NOLs will be applied to taxable income in 2006 prior to the Company&#146;s proposed  public offering and will be subject to additional IRS Section 382 limitations  subsequent to the Company&#146;s proposed public offering.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Discontinued  Activities.&#160; </i>The Company sold its directional drilling  division on August 6, 2004 and the operations of that division are reported in  the financial statements in this Report as discontinued operations.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>Results of Operations</b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  following discussion includes the results of operations of Bobcat for the  period December 16, 2005 through December 31, 2005.&#160; For further information relating to the results of operations of  Bobcat prior to the completion of the acquisition through September 30, 2005  and pro forma financial information reflecting the combined results of  operations of the Company and Bobcat for the nine months ended September 30,  2005 and the year ended December 31, 2004, see the Company&#146;s Amendment No. 1 to  its Current Report on Form 8-K filed on February 22, 2006.&#160; See also Note 2 to the Notes to Financial  Statements For the Years Ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003 included in  this Report for the pro forma statements of operations of the Company and  Bobcat for the years ended December 31, 2005 and 2004.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Year  Ended December 31, 2005 Compared to Year Ended December 31, 2004</i></b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Revenues</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company&#146;s total revenues increased by approximately $20.0 million for the year  ended December 31, 2005, as compared to 2004.&#160;  The pricing and utilization of the Company&#146;s services improved due to  the increase in well maintenance and drilling activity caused by higher natural  gas and oil prices.&#160; The Company also  added eight additional wireline units during the year ended December 31, 2005  as well as approximately $769,000 of revenues from Bobcat&#146;s operations  following the acquisition.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Operating Costs</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company&#146;s operating costs increased by approximately $9.1 million for the year  ended December 31, 2005 as compared to the same period of 2004.&#160; Operating costs were 59.0% of revenues for  the year ended December 31, 2005, as compared to 64.1% of revenues for  2004.&#160; The decrease in operating costs  as a percentage of revenues was primarily the result of the higher utilization  and pricing in the year ended December 31, 2005 compared with 2004.&#160; Salaries and benefits increased by  approximately $4.9 million </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">for the year ended December 31, 2005, as compared  to the same period in 2004.&#160; Total  number of employees increased from 313 at December 31, 2004 to approximately  480 at December 31, 2005, including approximately 80 employees from the Bobcat  acquisition.&#160; The increase in salaries  and benefits is primarily due to the increase in the number of employees in  2005 versus 2004.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Other Income (Expense)</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Other  income (expense) decreased by approximately $285,000 for the year ended  December 31, 2005, as compared to the same period in 2004.&#160; The decrease was primarily due to the  expensing of transaction expenses associated with a potential transaction which  was terminated in August 2005.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Income Taxes</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  provision for income taxes was approximately $175,000 in 2005 and $0 in  2004.&#160; The Company realized a net loss  for the year ended December 31, 2004, thereby generating additional NOLs.&#160; The Company recorded net income during the  year ended December 31, 2005, where NOLs were utilized to offset provision for  federal income taxes.&#160; The provision for  income taxes represents state income tax and alternative minimum tax  provisions.&#160; A full valuation allowance  has been recorded against the net deferred tax asset generated in prior years  from net operating losses to be carried forward.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Net Income</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net  income for the year ended December 31, 2005 was approximately $8.2 million  compared with a net loss of approximately $1.8 million for the same period of  2004.&#160; Included in 2004 results was a  loss from operations of the discontinued directional drilling segment of  approximately $1.7 million during the year ended December 31, 2004.&#160; The improved results for the year ended  December 31, 2005 over the same period in 2004 was primarily the result of an  increase in revenues resulting from an increase in demand for the Company&#146;s  services.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Discontinued Operations</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company sold its directional drilling division business on August 6, 2004 and  the operations of this division are reported in the financial statements  included in this Report as discontinued operations.&#160; The comparisons detailed above reflect the Company&#146;s continuing  operations.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Year  Ended December 31, 2004 Compared to Year Ended December 31, 2003</i></b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Revenues</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company&#146;s revenues from continuing operations increased by approximately $7.9  million or 17.3 % to $53.7 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2004 as  compared to revenues from continuing operations of $45.7 million for the year  ended December&nbsp;31, 2003.&#160; The  pricing and utilization of the Company&#146;s services improved due to the increase  in well maintenance and drilling activity caused by higher natural gas and oil  prices.&#160; The Company also averaged three  additional wireline units for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2004 as compared  to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2003.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Operating Costs</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating  costs increased by $4.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2004, as  compared to 2003.&#160; This increase was due  primarily to the increase in the Company&#146;s revenues and the level of the  Company&#146;s operations in 2004 as compared to 2003.&#160; Salaries and benefits increased by approximately $1.8 million for  2004 as compared to 2003.&#160; This was due  primarily to the Company&#146;s increased employee base.&#160; Operating costs as a percentage of revenues decreased to 64.1 %  in 2004 from 66.6 % in 2003 primarily because of the increased utilization of  the Company&#146;s assets as well as increases in pricing for the Company&#146;s  services.&#160; The increases in pricing were  largely the outgrowth of and were dependent upon the increase in demand for  services in the natural gas and oil well services sector.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Selling, General and Administrative Expenses</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Selling,  general and administrative expenses increased by approximately $209,000 to $9.5  million in 2004.&#160; As a percentage of  revenues, selling, general and administrative expenses decreased to 17.6 % in  2004 from 20.2 % in 2003, primarily as a result of the increased revenue level  generated in 2004 which did not require a corresponding increase in selling,  general and administrative expenses.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Depreciation and Amortization</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation  and amortization increased from $4.7 million in 2003 to $5.2 million in 2004,  primarily because of the increase in the Company&#146;s asset base resulting from  capital expenditures in the second half of 2003 and 2004.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Interest Expense</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest  expense and amortization of debt discount decreased by approximately $531,000  for 2004 as compared to 2003.&#160; This was  directly related to lower interest rates on outstanding senior debt in 2004 as  well as the reduced levels of senior debt outstanding in 2004.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Other Income</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net  gain on sale of fixed assets decreased in 2004 to a net gain of approximately  $53,000 from an approximate $239,000 net gain in 2003. Other income decreased  by approximately $98,000 in 2004.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Income Taxes</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  provision for income taxes was $0 in 2004 and 2003.&#160;&#160; A full valuation allowance has been recorded against the net  deferred tax assets generated each year from the net operating losses to be  carried forward.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Net Loss</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net  loss for 2004 was $1.8 million, compared with a net loss of $5.5 million in  2003. The improvement in the Company&#146;s results in 2004 over 2003 was primarily  attributable to the increased demand for the Company&#146;s services in 2004  primarily resulting from the improved commodities prices in 2004 and offset by  the impairment recorded of $1.4 million resulting from the sale of the  directional assets.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>Liquidity and Capital Resources</b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company&#146;s&#160; primary liquidity needs are  to fund capital expenditures, such as expanding its wireline and well  intervention services, geographic expansion, acquiring and upgrading trucks,  skids and snubbing units, the addition of complementary service lines and  funding general working capital needs. In addition, the Company needs capital  to fund strategic business acquisitions. The Company&#146;s primary sources of funds  have historically been cash flow from operations, proceeds from borrowings  under bank credit facilities and the issuance of debt. Upon completion of the  Company&#146;s proposed public offering, the Company anticipates that it will rely  on cash generated from operations, borrowings under its revolving credit  facility and possible debt and equity offerings to satisfy its liquidity needs.  The Company believes that with the current
and anticipated operating  environment of the natural gas and oil industry, it will be able to meet its liquidity  requirements for the remainder of 2006. In addition to funding operating  expenses, cash requirements for 2006 are expected to be comprised mainly of  amortization payments on indebtedness and funding capital improvements. The  Company&#146;s planned growth initiatives are expected to require capital  expenditures of in excess of $100 million over the next three years. The  Company&#146;s ability to fund planned capital expenditures and to make acquisitions  will depend upon its future operating performance, and more broadly, on the  availability of equity and debt financing, which will be affected by prevailing  economic conditions in the Company&#146;s industry, and general financial, business  and other factors, some of which are beyond the Company&#146;s control.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant  to employment contracts, the Company expects to make success bonus payments to  certain key employees immediately prior to or concurrently with the closing of  its proposed public offering in the aggregate amount of approximately $2.6  million of which approximately $1.5 million is accrued as of December 31, 2005.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company&#146;s outstanding indebtedness includes primarily senior indebtedness  aggregating approximately $55.2&nbsp;million at December 31, 2005, other  indebtedness of approximately $1.2 million and approximately $40.1&nbsp;million  (including approximately $18.2&nbsp;million of accrued interest) owing  primarily to the St. James Partnerships as well as other holders of  subordinated notes.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash  provided by the Company&#146;s operating activities was approximately $17.5 million  for the year ended December 31, 2005 as compared to cash provided of  approximately $3.6 million for the same period in 2004 The increase in cash  provided by operating activities was due mainly as a result in the increase in  demand for the Company&#146;s services. During the year ended December 31, 2005,  investing activities used cash of approximately $53.2 million for the  acquisition of Bobcat and $8.3 million for the acquisition of property, plant  and equipment as compared to $7.5 million for the same period in 2004, more  than offset by $10.4 million in proceeds from the sale of the Multishot  division. During the year ended December 31, 2005, financing activities used  cash of approximately $11.6 million for principal payments on debt and  approximately $2.5 million for debt issuance costs offset by
proceeds from bank  and other borrowings and net draws on working capital revolving loans of  approximately $56.2.&#160; In 2004, financing  activities used cash of approximately $23.0 million for principal payments on  debt and net payments on working capital revolving loans and other borrowings  and debt issuance costs of approximately $378,000 offset by proceeds from bank  and other borrowings of approximately $13.6 million.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash  provided by the Company&#146;s operating activities was approximately $3.5 million  for the year ended December 31, 2004 as compared to cash provided by operating  activities of $10.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2003.&#160; The decrease in cash provided by operating  activities was mainly a result of the change in the Company&#146;s prepaid assets  associated with the financing of insurance premiums, the assignment of current  assets and current liabilities in connection with the sale of the directional  drilling division and the timing of other current assets and liabilities.&#160; Investing activities used cash of  approximately $7.5 million during the year ended December 31, 2004 for the  acquisition of property, plant and equipment and was offset by proceeds from  the sale of discontinued operations and fixed assets of $10.7 million.&#160; During the year ended December 31,
2003,  acquisitions of property, plant and equipment used cash of $3.1 million offset  by proceeds of $685,000 from the sale of fixed assets.&#160; Financing activities during the year ended  December 31, 2004 provided cash of $13.6 million offset by principal payments  on long-term notes and the Company&#146;s working capital revolving loan of $23.0  million and debt issuance costs of approximately $378,000.&#160; Financing activities provided cash of $5.4  million from borrowings during the year ended December 31, 2003 offset by  principal payments on long-term notes and the Company&#146;s working capital  revolving loan of $10.3 million and debt issuance costs of approximately  $48,000.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During  the year ended December 31, 2005, the Company expended approximately $56.3  million for the acquisition of Bobcat financed under the Company&#146;s Senior  Secured Credit Agreement and approximately $961,000 for other property, plant  and equipment financed under notes payable.&#160;  During the year ended December 31, 2004, the Company expended  approximately $841,000 for the acquisition of property, plant and equipment  financed under notes payable.&#160; During  the year ended December 31, 2003, the Company expended $3.3 million for the  acquisition of property, plant and equipment financed under the Company&#146;s  Senior Secured Credit Agreement and notes payable.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>Description of the Company&#146;s Indebtedness </i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Senior  Secured Credit Agreement</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On  December 16, 2005, the Company entered into the Senior Secured Credit Agreement  with GECC, providing for a term loan and revolving and capital expenditure  credit facilities in an aggregate amount of $50.0 million. The Senior Secured  Credit Agreement amended, restated and modified the credit agreement the  Company entered into with GECC as of September 14, 2001 and as it was amended  and restated on November 14, 2004, including the amendments thereto. The Senior  Secured Credit Agreement includes:</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

  </td>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Eligible  accounts receivable are accounts in which the Company has an interest  excluding, among other items and, subject to certain exceptions, debtors&#146;  accounts outstanding that are not paid within the earlier of 60 days past the  due date or 90 days following the original invoice date, accounts of debtors  that have suspended business or commenced various insolvency proceedings and  accounts to the extent the account exceeds the credit limit established by GECC  in its reasonable credit judgment. GECC has the right to establish, modify and  eliminate reserves against eligible accounts receivable from time to time in  its reasonable judgment.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;GECC&#146;s  agreement to make revolving loans expires on December 16, 2008 and its  agreement to make capital expenditure loans expires on December 16, 2006,  unless earlier terminated under the terms of the Senior Secured Credit  Agreement.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest  Rates.</i> Initially, as  of the closing, the annual interest rate on borrowings under the revolving loan  facility is 0.75% above the index rate, and the annual interest rate on  borrowings under the term loan and capital expenditure loan facility is 2.25%  above the index rate. The index rate is a floating rate equal to the higher of  (i) the rate publicly quoted from time to time by the Wall Street Journal as  the prime rate, or (ii) the average of the rates on overnight Federal funds  transactions among members of the Federal Reserve System plus 0.5%. The  interest rate margin above the index rate may be adjusted from time to time on  a quarterly basis based on the Company&#146;s ratio of its funded debt to EBITDA for  the trailing twelve months prior to the determination. Subject to the absence  of an event of default and fulfillment of certain other conditions, the Company  can
elect to borrow or convert any loan and pay the annual interest at the  LIBOR rate plus applicable margins of 2.25% on the revolving loan and 3.75% on  the term loan and capital expenditure loan. If an event of default in the  nature of a failure to make any payment of principal of, interest on or fees  owing in respect to loans when due and payable or the commencement of  bankruptcy proceedings involving the Company has occurred, the annual interest  rate is increased by 2% and, if any other default or event of default has  occurred and is continuing, GECC may elect to increase the interest rate by  that amount.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Collateral.</i> Advances under the Senior Secured Credit  Agreement are collateralized by a senior lien against substantially all of the  Company&#146;s assets.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Use  of Proceeds.</i> Initial  borrowings under the Senior Secured Credit Agreement advanced on December 16,  2005 were $1.3 million borrowed under the revolving loan and $30.0 million  under the term loan. No</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">33</font></div>

<div  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">borrowings were made under the capital  expenditure loan facility. The proceeds of the term loan were used to pay a  portion of the Bobcat acquisition purchase price, related fees and expenses and  repayment of substantially all Bobcat indebtedness, and approximately $2.1  million was placed in escrow for the repayment of principal and accrued  interest on subordinated secured indebtedness and approximately $2.8 million  was used for general corporate purposes.<b>&#160; </b>The  outstanding balance of approximately $6.3 million under the Company&#146;s previous  credit agreement with GECC was paid out of the Company&#146;s existing cash.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Maturity  of Loans.</i> Borrowings  under the revolving loan are able to be repaid and re-borrowed from time to  time for working capital and general corporate needs, subject to the Company&#146;s  continuing compliance with the terms of the agreement. Any amounts outstanding  under the revolving loan are due and payable on December 16, 2008. The term  loan is to be repaid in 12 consecutive quarterly installments of $1.1 million  commencing January 1, 2006 with a final installment of $16.8 million due and  payable on January 1, 2009. The capital expenditure loan is to be repaid in  eight consecutive quarterly installments with each quarterly installment equal  to 1/20th of the borrowings funded prior to the expiration of the one-year term  of the facility and with a final installment in the amount of the remaining  principal balance due on December 16, 2008.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Mandatory  and Voluntary Prepayments.</i> Borrowings under the Senior Secured Credit Agreement are subject to  certain mandatory pre-payments including, among other requirements, pre-payment  out of a portion of the net proceeds of any sale of stock by the Company in a  public offering. The Company must apply the net proceeds from any sale of its  stock, other than on exercise of existing warrants and conversion rights,  occurring before December 31, 2006 to the prepayment of loans. Such cash  proceeds, after deduction of underwriting discounts and commissions and other  reasonable costs the Company incurs are to be applied to the prepayment of (i)  loans outstanding under the Company&#146;s Senior Secured Credit Agreement, (ii)  loans outstanding under the Company&#146;s Second Lien Credit Agreement, and (iii)  to prepay or redeem all the Company&#146;s outstanding subordinated notes and shares
of its common stock owned by St. James Capital Partners, L.P., SJMB, L.P. and  other holders of the Company&#146;s subordinated secured notes as of December 16,  2005, the shares of the Company&#146;s common stock issued in exchange for warrants,  subordinated notes and other convertible securities pursuant to the recapitalization  agreements the Company entered into in October 2005, a fee in the amount of  $274,000 owing to SJMB, L.P. and &#147;Change of Control&#148; payments in the aggregate  amount of approximately $2.6 million the Company is required to make under the  terms of employment agreements with certain of the Company&#146;s employees, as the  term &#147;Change of Control&#148; is defined in those agreements (herein, amounts to be  paid under this subsection (iii) are referred to as &#147;Junior Capital&#148;), in the  following manner:</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">To the extent the Junior Capital is paid or  repurchased in full under the foregoing provisions prior to the prepayment in  full of loans outstanding under the Company&#146;s Credit Agreements, the remaining  net proceeds are to be allocated 50% to loans outstanding under the Company&#146;s  Credit Agreements. If any event of default has occurred under the Company&#146;s  Senior Secured Credit Agreement and is continuing, and the Company has been  notified in writing of such event of default (or the Company has been notified  in writing of the equivalent event of default under the Second Lien Credit  Agreement), at the time the Company receives the net proceeds, 100% of such net  proceeds are to be allocated to the loans outstanding under the Company&#146;s  Senior Secured Credit Agreement, without application of any portion thereof to  Junior Capital or loans under the Second Lien Credit Agreement.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company has proposed to GECC that the Senior Secured Credit Agreement and  Second Lien Credit Agreement be amended to provide that 100% of the net  proceeds realized from its proposed public offering that is to be applied to  the repayment of indebtedness owing to GECC be allocated to the repayment of  indebtedness outstanding under the Second Lien Credit Agreement and -0-% be  allocated to the repayment of indebtedness outstanding under the Senior Secured  Credit Agreement.&#160; The Company is  awaiting a definitive response from GECC regarding this proposal.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;If  the Company issues any shares of common stock, other than as described above,  or any debt at any time, the Company is required to prepay the loans  outstanding under the Senior Secured Credit Agreement in an amount equal to all  such proceeds, net of underwriting discounts and commissions and other  reasonable costs.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company is also required to prepay annually, commencing with the fiscal year  ending December 31, 2006, loans and other outstanding obligations under the  Senior Secured Credit Agreement in an amount equal to 75% of the Company&#146;s  excess cash flow for the immediately preceding fiscal year. Excess cash flow is  defined, with respect to any fiscal year, as the Company&#146;s net income plus  depreciation, amortization and interest expense, to the extent deducted in  determining net income, minus capital expenditures, minus interest expense paid  or accrued and scheduled principal payments paid or payable, plus or minus,  extraordinary gains or losses which are cash items not included in net income,  plus taxes deducted in determining net income to the extent not paid in cash.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Any  mandatory prepayments made as provided above are to be applied substantially as  follows: first, to any fees then due and payable to GECC, second, to interest  then due and payable on the term loan and capital expenditure loan, pro rata  between the term loan and capital expenditure loan, third, to prepay the  scheduled principal installments on the term loan and capital expenditure loan,  allocated pro rata between the term loan and capital expenditure loan, and  applied to principal installments in inverse order of maturity, until the term  loan and capital expenditure loan have been prepaid in full; fourth, to  interest then due and payable on the revolving loan; and fifth, to the  principal balance of the revolving loan until the same shall have been paid in  full. The revolving loan is permanently reduced by the amount of any such  prepayments.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company may at any time prepay all or part of the term loan or capital  expenditure loan, permanently reduce or terminate the capital expenditure  commitment, and permanently reduce but not terminate the revolving loan  commitment provided such prepayments or reductions are in the minimum amount of  $500,000 and integral multiples of $250,000, subject to the payment of certain  pre-payment fees declining from 1.0% in the event the termination or reduction  occurs during the first year, 0.5% in the event the termination or reduction  occurs during the second year, and 0.25% in the event the termination or  reduction occurs during the third year of the term of the Senior Secured Credit  Agreement. The Company is required to use, subject to certain exceptions, the  net proceeds from the sale of any assets or the stock of any subsidiary to  prepay all borrowings under the facilities. The Company is
required to repay  any borrowings in excess of the applicable borrowing availability, including  borrowings under the term loan in excess of 70% of the forced liquidation value  of eligible term loan equipment. The forced liquidation value </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Events  of Default.</i> Events of  default under the Senior Secured Credit Agreement include, among others and  subject to certain limitations, (a) the failure to make any payment of  principal, interest, or fees when due and payable or to pay or reimburse GECC  for any expense reimbursable under the Senior Secured Credit Agreement within  ten days of demand for payment, (b) the failure to perform the covenants under  the Senior Secured Credit Agreement relating to use of proceeds, maintenance of  a cash management system, maintenance of insurance, delivery of certificates of  title for equipment, delivery of certain post-closing documents, and  maintenance of compliance with the Senior Secured Credit Agreement&#146;s negative  covenants, (c) the failure to deliver to the lenders monthly un-audited,  quarterly un-audited and annual audited financial statements, an annual  operating plan, and other
reports, certificates and information as required by  the Senior Secured Credit Agreement, (d) the failure to perform any other  provision of the Senior Secured Credit Agreement (other than those set forth in  (b) above) which nonperformance remains un-remedied for 20 days or more, (e) a  default or breach under any other agreement or instrument to which the Company  is a party beyond any grace period that involves the failure to pay in excess  of $250,000 or causes or permits to cause indebtedness in excess of $250,000 to  become due prior to its stated maturity, (f) any information in a borrowing  base certificate or any representation or warranty or certificate or in any  written statement report, or financial statement delivered to GECC being untrue  or incorrect in any material respect, (g) a change of control, as defined, of  the Company, (h) the occurrence of an event having a material adverse effect,  (i) the initiation of insolvency, bankruptcy or liquidation proceedings, (j)  any final
judgment for the payment of money in excess of $250,000 is  outstanding against the Company and is not within thirty days discharged,  stayed or bonded pending appeal, (k) any material provision of or lien under  any document relating to the Senior Secured Credit Agreement ceases to be  valid, (l) the attachment, seizure or levy upon of the Company&#146;s assets which  continues for 30 days or more, and (m) William Jenkins ceases to serve as the  Company&#146;s chief executive officer, unless otherwise agreed by GECC. Upon the  occurrence of a default, which is defined as any event that with the passage of  time or notice or both would, unless waived or cured, become an event of  default, or event of default, the lenders may discontinue making revolving  loans and capital expenditure loans to the Company and increase the interest  rate on all loans. Upon the occurrence of an event of default, the lenders may  terminate the Senior Secured Credit Agreement, declare all indebtedness  outstanding under
the Senior Secured Credit Agreement due and payable, and  exercise any of their rights under the Senior Secured Credit Agreement which  includes the ability to foreclose on the Company&#146;s assets. In the event of a  bankruptcy or liquidation proceeding, all borrowings under the Senior Secured  Credit Agreement are immediately due and payable.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Second  Lien Credit Agreement</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Term Loan.</i> On  December 16, 2005, the Company entered into the Second Lien Credit Agreement  with GECC, providing for a term loan $25.0 million.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest  Rate.</i> The annual  interest rate on borrowings under the term loan is 6.0% above the index rate.  The index rate is a floating rate equal to the higher of (i) the rate publicly  quoted from time to time by the Wall Street Journal as the prime rate, or (ii)  the average of the rates on overnight Federal funds transactions among members  of the Federal Reserve System plus 0.5%. Subject to the absence of an event of  default and fulfillment of certain other conditions, the Company can elect to  borrow or convert any loan and pay the annual interest at the LIBOR rate plus a  margin of 7.5%. If an event of default in the nature of a failure to make any payment  of principal of, interest on or fees owing in respect to loans when due and  payable or the commencement of bankruptcy proceedings involving the Company has  occurred, the annual interest </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;If  the Company issues any shares of common stock, other than as described above in  a public offering of the Company&#146;s securities, or any debt at any time, the  Company is required to prepay the loans outstanding under the Second Lien  Credit Agreement in an amount equal to all such proceeds, net of underwriting  discounts and commissions and other reasonable costs.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Any  mandatory prepayments made as provided above are to be applied substantially as  follows: first, to any fees then due and payable to GECC, second, to interest  then due and payable on the loan and, third, to prepay the principal of the  loan.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company may at any time prepay all or part of the loan or capital expenditure  loan, subject to the payment of certain pre-payment fees declining from 2.0% in  during the first year, 1.0% during the second year, and 0.5% in the event the  termination or reduction occurs during the third year of the term of the Second  Lien Credit Agreement. The Company is required to use, subject to certain  exceptions, the net proceeds from the sale of any assets or the stock of any  subsidiary to prepay all borrowings under the facilities.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Recently  Issued Accounting Pronouncements </i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On  December 21, 2004, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued Staff Position (FSP) FAS  109-1, <i>Application  of FASB Statement No. 109, Accounting for Income Taxes</i>, to the Tax  Deduction on Qualified Production Activities Provided by the American Jobs  Creation Act of 2004, was issued. FSP FAS 109-1 clarifies that this tax  deduction should be accounted for as a special deduction in accordance with  Statement 109.&#160; As such, the special  deduction has no effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities existing at the  date of enactment.&#160; Rather, the impact  of this deduction will be reported in the period in which the deduction is  claimed on the Company&#146;s tax return beginning in 2005.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In  December 2004, the FASB issued SFAS 123 (revised 2004), <i>Share-Based Payment</i> (SFAS  No. 123(R)).&#160; This Statement requires  that the costs of employee share-based payments be measured at fair value on  the awards&#146; grant date using an option-pricing model and recognized in the  financial statements over the requisite service period.&#160; This Statement does not change the  accounting for stock ownership plans, which are subject to American Institute  of Certified Public Accountants SOP 93-6, <i>Employer&#146;s Accounting for Employee Stock Ownership  Plans</i>.&#160; Statement 123(R)  supersedes Opinion 25, <i>Accounting for Stock Issued to Employees</i>  and its related interpretations, and eliminates the alternative to use Opinion  25&#146;s intrinsic value method of accounting, which the Company is currently  using.&#160; Certain stock awards may be  considered liabilities
instead of equity components under SFAS No. 123(R).</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;SFAS  No. 123(R) allows for two alternative transition methods.&#160; The first method is the modified prospective  application whereby compensation cost for the portion of awards for which the  requisite service has not yet been rendered that are outstanding as of the  adoption date will be recognized over the remaining service period.&#160; The compensation cost for that portion of  awards will be based on the grant-date fair value of those awards as calculated  for pro forma disclosures under SFAS No. 123, as originally issued.&#160; All new awards and awards that are modified,  repurchased, or cancelled after the adoption date will be accounted for under  the provisions of SFAS No. 123(R).&#160; The  second method is the modified retrospective application, which requires that  the Company restate prior period financial statements.&#160; The modified </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">42</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><a href="#Contents">Back to Contents</a></b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">retrospective application may be applied  either to all prior periods or only to prior interim periods in the year of  adoption of this statement.&#160; The Company  adopted the modified prospective application method on January 1, 2006 and does  not expect a material impact on its financial statements.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In  November 2004, the FASB issued SFAS No. 151, <i>Inventory Costs, an amendment of ARB  No. 43, Chapter 4</i>, which is effective for inventory costs incurred  during fiscal years beginning after June 15, 2005.&#160; The amendments made by SFAS No. 151 will improve financial  reporting by clarifying that abnormal amounts of idle facility expense,  freight, handling costs, and wasted materials (spoilage) should be recognized  as current-period charges and by requiring the allocation of fixed production  overheads to inventory based on the normal capacity of the production  facilities.&#160; The adoption of Statement  151 did not have a significant effect on the Company&#146;s financial statements.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In  December 2003, the FASB issued Interpretation No. 46 (revised December 2003)  (&#147;FIN 46(R)&#148;), <i>Consolidation of Variable Interest Entities, an interpretation of ARB  51</i>. The primary objectives of FIN 46R are to provide guidance on the  identification of entities for which control is achieved through means other  than through voting rights (&#147;variable interest entities&#148; or &#147;VIEs&#148;) and how to  determine if a business enterprise should consolidate the VIEs. This new model  for consolidation applies to an entity for which either: the equity investors  (if any) do not have a controlling financial interest; or the equity investment  at risk is insufficient to finance the entity&#146;s activities without receiving  additional subordinated financial support from other parties. In addition, FIN  46(R) requires that all enterprises with a significant variable interest in a
 VIE make additional disclosures regarding their relationship with the VIE. The  interpretation requires public entities to apply FIN 46(R) to all entities that  are considered Special Purpose Entities in practice and under the FASB  literature that was applied before the issuance of FIN 46(R). The adoption of  FIN 46R had no effect on the Company&#146;s financial statements.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant  Accounting Policies</i></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of  Operations is based upon its financial statements, which have been prepared in  accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the U.S. The  preparation of these financial statements requires the Company to make  estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets,  liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosures of contingent  assets and liabilities. On an on-going basis, the Company evaluates its estimates,  including those related to the allowance for bad debts, inventory, long-lived  assets, intangibles and goodwill. The Company bases its estimates on historical  experience and on various other assumptions that are believed to be reasonable  under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making  judgments about the carrying value of assets and liabilities
that are not  readily apparent from other sources. Actual results may differ from these  estimates under different assumptions or conditions.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Allowance  for Doubtful Accounts</i>  &#151; The Company&#146;s allowance for doubtful accounts is maintained at an amount  equal to estimated losses in its accounts receivable.&#160; The Company continually monitors the accounts receivable from its  customers for any collectability issues.&#160;  An allowance for doubtful accounts is established based on reviews of  individual customer accounts, recent loss experience, current economic  conditions, and other pertinent factors.&#160;  Accounts deemed uncollectible are charged to the allowance.&#160; Provisions for bad debts and recoveries on  accounts previously charged off are added to the allowance.&#160; All accounts outstanding more than 30 days  are considered past due.&#160; </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Long-Lived  Assets</i> &#151; In  accordance with SFAS No. 144 <i>Accounting for the Impairment or Disposal of  Long-Lived Assets</i>, the Company recognizes impairment losses on  long-lived assets used in operations when indicators of impairment are present  and the undiscounted cash flows over the life of the assets are less than the  asset&#146;s carrying amount. If an impairment exists, the amount of such impairment  is calculated </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">43</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<hr noshade align="center" width="100%" size="2">
<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>

<div><a name="we_044"></a><font  size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><a href="#Contents">Back to Contents</a></b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">based on projections of future discounted  cash flows. These projections use a discount rate and terminal value multiple  that would be customary for evaluating current natural gas and oil services  company transactions.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Goodwill  and Intangible Assets </i><font face=Symbol><i>&#190;</i></font><i>&#160; </i>Goodwill is stated at cost.&#160; The Company implemented SFAS No. 142, <i>Goodwill and  Other Intangible Assets</i> on January 1, 2002 and ceased amortization  of goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets.&#160; SFAS No. 142 requires an assessment of potential impairment upon  adoption and annually thereafter in the month it elected to perform its  analysis or more frequently if events or circumstances indicate that an  impairment may have occurred.&#160;  Intangible assets are stated at cost and are amortized over their  estimated useful lives.&#160; Intangible  assets are subject to an assessment of potential impairment whenever events or  circumstances indicate that an impairment may have occurred. </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company considers external factors in making its assessment. Specifically,  changes in oil prices and other economic conditions surrounding the industry,  consolidation within the industry, competition from other natural gas and oil  well services providers, the ability to employ and maintain a skilled  workforce, and other pertinent factors are among the factors that could lead  its management to reassess the reliability of its goodwill and intangible  assets.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Property  and Equipment</i> &#151;  Property and equipment are carried at original cost less applicable  depreciation.&#160; Depreciation is  recognized on the straight line basis over lives ranging from two to ten years.&#160; Major renewals and improvements are  capitalized and depreciated over each asset&#146;s estimated remaining useful life.  Maintenance and repair costs are charged to expense as incurred. When assets  are sold or retired, the remaining costs and related accumulated depreciation  are removed from the accounts and any resulting gain or loss is included in  income. Property and equipment held and used by the Company is reviewed for  impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the  carrying amounts may not be recoverable. The Company estimates the future  undiscounted cash flows of the affected assets to determine the recoverability  of carrying
amounts.&#160; </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue  Recognition </i><font face=Symbol><i>&#190;</i></font><i>&#160; </i>The Company derives revenues from performance  of services and the sale of equipment.&#160;  Service revenues are recognized at the time services are performed.&#160; The Company&#146;s sales are not usually subject  to rights of return, and historically, sales returns have not been significant.  Revenue related to equipment sales is recognized when the equipment has been  shipped and title and risk of loss has been passed to the customer.&#160; Deferred revenue, net of deferred related  cost of sales, is recorded as unearned revenues in the Company&#146;s balance sheet  based on the relative days completed on the job to total required.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Income  Taxes</i> &#151; The Company  accounts for income taxes under an asset and liability approach that requires  the recognition of deferred tax assets and liabilities for the expected future  tax consequences of events that have been recognized in its financial  statements or tax returns.&#160; In  estimating future tax consequences, the Company generally considers all  expected future events other than enactments of changes in tax laws or rates.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company had no off-balance sheet arrangements as of December 31, 2004 and 2005.</font></div>

  </td>
  <td width="90%" valign="top">
  <div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk</b></font></div>
  </td>
 </tr>
</table>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;From  time to time, the Company holds financial instruments comprised of debt  securities and time deposits.&#160; All such  instruments are classified as securities available for sale.&#160; The Company does not invest in portfolio  equity securities, or commodities, or use financial derivatives for trading or  hedging purposes.&#160; The Company&#146;s debt  security portfolio represents funds held temporarily pending use in its  business and operations.&#160; The Company  manages these funds accordingly.&#160; The  Company seeks reasonable assuredness of the safety of principal and market  liquidity by investing in rated fixed income securities while, at the </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">44</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">same time, seeking to achieve a favorable  rate of return.&#160; Its market risk  exposure consists of exposure to changes in interest rates and to the risks of  changes in the credit quality of issuers.&#160;  The Company typically invest in investment grade securities with a term  of three years or less.&#160; The Company  believes that any exposure to interest rate risk is not material.&#160; At December 31, 2005, the Company held no  investments.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Under  the Company&#146;s Credit Agreements with GECC, it is subject to market risk  exposure related to changes in the prime interest rate.&#160; Assuming the Company&#146;s level of borrowings  from GECC at December 31, 2005 remained unchanged throughout 2006, if a 100  basis point increase in interest rates under the Credit Agreements from rates  in existence at December 31, 2005 prevailed throughout the year 2006, it would  increase the Company&#146;s 2006 interest expense by approximately $552,000.&#160; The foregoing does not give effect to any  repayment of outstanding indebtedness under the Company&#146;s Credit Agreements out  of the net proceeds it may realize in its proposed public offering.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Set  forth below is the description of the backgrounds of the Company&#146;s directors,  executive officers and proposed directors.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;William  L. Jenkins</i></b> has  been the Company&#146;s Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer since March  1989.&#160; From 1973 until 1980, Mr. Jenkins  held a variety of field engineering and training positions with Welex - A  Halliburton Company, in the South and Southwest.&#160; From 1980 until March 1989, Mr. Jenkins worked with Triad Oil  &amp; Gas, Inc., as a consultant, providing services to a number of natural gas  and oil companies.&#160; During that time,  Mr. Jenkins was involved in the organization of a number of drilling and oil  field service companies, including a predecessor of the Company&#146;s, of which he  served as Secretary/Treasurer until 1988.&#160;  Mr. Jenkins has over 30 years of experience in the oil field service  business.&#160; </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Robert  J. McNally</i></b> is the  Company&#146;s Executive Vice President of Operations and Finance and has been  employed by the Company and has served as a Director since January 2006.&#160; From 1994 through 2000, Mr. McNally held a  variety of field engineering, sales and marketing positions with Schlumberger  Ltd.&#160; From July of 2000 through the end  of 2005, Mr. McNally was an Associate and then Vice President of Simmons &amp;  Company International, a leading energy investment bank, in its corporate  finance department, primarily providing investment banking and corporate  finance advisory services to oilfield service companies.&#160; As an employee of Simmons &amp; Company  International, Mr.&nbsp;McNally served as the Company&#146;s primary financial  advisor from 2001 through 2005.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Ron  E. Whitter</i></b> has been the Company&#146;s Chief Financial  Officer since August 1999.&#160; Prior to  joining the Company, Mr. Whitter was employed by Oil States as Divisional  Controller.&#160; From 1987 until 1993, Mr.  Whitter was employed by Norfolk Energy as Financial Accounting Manager and was  employed by Transco Energy from 1985 to 1987.&#160;  Mr.&nbsp;Whitter is a C.P.A.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Charles  E. Underbrink</i></b> was  elected a Director in April, 1998.&#160; For  more than the past five years, he has been employed as the Chairman of St.  James Capital Corp. and SJMB, L.L.C., Houston based merchant</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">47</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<hr noshade align="center" width="100%" size="2">
<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><a href="#Contents">Back to Contents</a></b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">banking firms.&#160; From the inception of St. James Capital Corp. and SJMB, L.L.C.  until March 1, 2001 he also served as the Chief Executive Officer of each.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;James  H. Harrison </i></b>was elected a Director in March, 2003.&#160; He is the Chief Financial Officer of  St.&nbsp;James Capital Corp. and SJMB, L.L.C., Houston-based merchant banking  firms.&#160; Prior to joining St.&nbsp;James  Capital Corp. and SJMB, L.L.C. in January of 1998, he served as a manager in  the Assurance division of Ernst &amp; Young LLP, a national public accounting  firm.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>Proposed Directors:</b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gerald  M. Hage </i></b>is expected to be elected as a Director prior  to the closing of the Company&#146;s proposed public offering.&#160; Mr. Hage has been an independent oil service  consultant since 1988.&#160; From 1994 to  1998, he served as Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Phoenix Energy Services,  a provider of maintenance, inspection and emergency services to the natural gas  industry.&#160; From 1988 to 1994, he was  President and Chief Executive Officer of Total Energy Services, a drilling and  production-services company.&#160; From 1980  to 1988, Mr. Hage served as President of certain affiliates of Baker Hughes,  Inc.&#160; From 1971 to 1980, he was Vice  President, Manufacturing of International Harvester.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Robert  L. Hollier</i></b> is  expected to be elected as a Director prior to the closing of the Company&#146;s  proposed public offering.&#160; From February  2004 until November 2005, Mr. Hollier was a Partner and Director of Lone Star  Fasteners, L.P., a manufacturer of bolting products for the energy  industry.&#160; From August 2002 through  December 2005, Mr. Hollier was a Partner and Executive Director of Monosep,  Inc., a provider of water process and separation technology equipment and  services.&#160; In August 1979, Mr. Hollier  founded OSCA, Inc., a Gulf of Mexico region provider of pressure pumping  services, completion tools and completion fluids, and served as its President  and Chief Executive Officer until June 2002.&#160;  From 1970 to 1979, he served as Vice President and Chief Operating  Officer of Gulf Coast Drilling Fluids, Inc.&#160;  From 1963 to 1970, he was employed by
Amoco Production Company.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;John  T. McNabb, II</i></b> is  expected to be elected as a Director prior to the closing of the Company&#146;s  proposed public offering.&#160; Since March  1992, Mr. McNabb has served as Chairman of Growth Capital Partners, L.P., a  merchant banking firm that provides financial advisory services to middle  market companies throughout the United States.&#160;  And since 2001, he has served as a Principal of Southwest Mezzanine  Investments, the investment affiliate of Growth Capital Partners, L.P.&#160; Prior thereto, Mr. McNabb was a Managing  Director of Bankers Trust New York Corporation and a board member of BT  Southwest, Inc., the southwest U.S. merchant banking affiliate of Bankers  Trust.&#160; Mr. McNabb has also been  employed by the merchant banking and corporate finance affiliates of The Prudential  Insurance Company of America and by the Exploration and Production Division of
Mobil Oil Corporation.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>Composition of the Board After the Company&#146;s Proposed Public  Offering</b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Currently,  the St. James Partnerships have the authority to designate one person to serve  on the Company&#146;s board.&#160; However, the  Company and the St. James Partnerships have agreed to terminate this agreement  and, prior to the closing of the Company&#146;s proposed public offering, the  Company expects to elect Messrs. Hage, Hollier and McNabb to its board to serve  as independent directors.&#160; Messrs.  Underbrink and Harrison are expected to resign as directors prior to the  closing of the Company&#146;s proposed public offering.&#160; </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>Committees</b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Audit  Committee.</i> The Company&#146;s board of directors has  appointed an audit committee consisting of Messrs. Jenkins, Underbrink and  Harrison.&#160; The Company&#146;s audit  committee, among other things, meets with the Company&#146;s independent registered  public accounting firm to review its accounting policies, internal controls and  other accounting and auditing matters; approves the engagement of its  independent registered public accounting firm; and reviews the engagement and  fees relating to the annual audit, special audit work and non-audit services  which may be recommended or required by the independent registered </font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">48</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<hr noshade align="center" width="100%" size="2">
<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><a href="#Contents">Back to Contents</a></b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">public accounting firm.&#160; The  Company&#146;s securities are not currently listed on a registered national  securities exchange or in an automated inter-dealer quotation system and, accordingly,  it is not subject to the listing standards imposed by rules adopted under the  U.S. Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to  the closing of the Company&#146;s proposed public offering, the Company expects that  the current members of its audit committee will resign from its audit committee  and that its Board of Directors will appoint Messrs. Hage, Hollier and McNabb,  who are expected to be elected Directors prior to the closing of the Company&#146;s  proposed public offering, to its audit committee.&#160; Each of such persons is expected to be determined to be an  &#147;independent director&#148; under the rules of the Nasdaq Stock Market.&#160; The Company also intends to adopt a new  audit committee charter, under which its audit committee&#146;s responsibilities  will include, among other responsibilities, (i) the appointment, compensation  and oversight of the work performed by its registered public accounting firm,  (ii) the adoption and assurance of compliance with a pre-approval policy with  respect to
services provided by its registered public accounting firm, at least  annually, (iii) the review of a report by its registered public accounting firm  as to relationships between the registered public accounting firm and the  Company so as to assure the independence of its registered public accounting  firm, (iv) the review of the annual audited and quarterly financial statements  with the Company&#146;s management and its registered public accounting firm, and  (v)&nbsp;discuss with its  registered public accounting firm their required disclosure relating to the  conduct of the audit, and (vi) implementation of and compliance with the  Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Nominating  Committee</i>.&#160; Prior to the closing of the Company&#146;s  proposed public offering, the Company will establish a nominating committee  consisting entirely of independent directors.&#160;  The Company expects the board to appoint Messrs. Hage, Hollier and  McNabb to serve on this committee.&#160; The  principal duty of the nominating committee is to recommend to the board of directors  proposed nominees for election to the board of directors by the stockholders at  annual meetings, including an annual review as to the renominations of  incumbents and proposed nominees for election by the board of directors to fill  vacancies that occur between stockholder meetings.&#160; It is intended that the Company&#146;s board of directors will adopt  prior to the closing of the Company&#146;s proposed public offering a written  charter for the nominating committee.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Compensation  Committee.&#160; </i>Prior to the closing of the Company&#146;s  proposed public offering, the Company will establish a compensation committee  comprised entirely of independent directors.&#160;  The Company expects the board to appoint Messrs. Hage, Hollier and  McNabb to serve on this committee.&#160; The  compensation committee will administer the Company&#146;s stock plans and incentive  compensation plans, including its 2000 Stock Incentive Plan, and in this  capacity will make all option grants or awards to the Company&#146;s directors and  employees under such plans. In addition, the compensation committee will be  responsible for making recommendations to the board of directors with respect  to the compensation of its chief executive officer and its other executive  officers and for establishing compensation and employee benefit policies.&#160; It is intended that the
Company&#146;s board of  directors will adopt prior to the closing of the Company&#146;s proposed public  offering a written charter for the compensation committee.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>Compliance with Section 16(a) of the Securities Exchange Act  of 1934</b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Section  16(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 requires the Company&#146;s officers  and Directors, and persons who beneficially own more than ten percent (10%) of a  registered class of its equity securities, to file reports of ownership and  changes in ownership with the SEC.&#160;  Officers, directors and beneficial owners of more than ten percent (10%)  of the Company&#146;s Common Stock are required by SEC regulations to furnish the  Company with copies of all Section 16(a) forms that they file.&#160; To the best of the Company&#146;s knowledge,  based solely on a review of such reports as filed with the SEC, all such  persons have complied with such reporting requirements during the Company&#146;s  most recent fiscal year.</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>Employment Agreements</b></font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></div>

<div><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The  Company has entered into an employment agreement with Mr. William L. Jenkins,  its President and Chief Executive Officer, the term of which was extended in  March 2005 and December 2005 and currently expires on April 1, 2009.&#160; Under the agreement, Mr. Jenkins serves as  President, Chief Executive Officer and a Director.&#160; Mr. Jenkins receives a base salary of not less than $350,000 per  year and was granted warrants to purchase 250,000 shares of the Company&#146;s common  stock at an exercise price of $7.50 per share.&#160;  If the Company achieves, during any calendar quarter during the period  of Mr. Jenkins&#146; employment, a ratio of EBITDA to sales of 20% or more, Mr.  Jenkins will be paid a bonus for the quarter equal to 1% of the Company&#146;s  EBITDA during the quarter.&#160; In the event  of a Change of Control, as defined, the Company agrees that the employment  agreement
will terminate and Mr. Jenkins will be paid a sum equal to three  times the compensation paid to Mr. Jenkins during the 12 months preceding the  Change of Control.&#160; A Change of Control  is defined in the agreement as any of the following occurring after January 1,  2005: any person or group of persons acquiring 20% or more of the Company&#146;s  outstanding shares of voting capital stock, the sale of more than 25% of its  assets in a single or series of related transactions, a merger of the Company  with any other person or firm, during any period of 12 consecutive calendar  months, the individuals who were Directors at the beginning of such period  (including Directors whose election or nomination for election was approved by  at least two-thirds of the Directors then in office who were Directors at the  beginning of the period or whose election was so approved) cease for any reason  other than death or disability to constitute a majority of the Directors then  in office, St. James Capital Corp.
ceases to be the general partner, managing  partner or otherwise ceases to control St. James</font></div>
